question: How much was the literacy rate of India as per census 1951?
solution:
The Correct answer is __**0.1833**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• As per the **Census of 1951**, the literacy rate in India was recorded as **18.33%**, which corresponds to the value **0.1833** in decimal form.
 
• The 1951 census was the first census conducted in independent India, and it provided crucial insights into the country's **demographic and socio-economic conditions**.
 
• The literacy rate is calculated as the percentage of people aged seven and above who can read and write with understanding.
 
• The literacy rate of 18.33% highlighted the challenges in education and marked the beginning of efforts to improve literacy under the **Five-Year Plans** and other government initiatives.
 
• The 1951 census also emphasized the need for policies to enhance education access, particularly in rural and underprivileged areas.
 
• Post-independence, India saw the establishment of institutions like **NCERT (National Council of Educational Research and Training)** and the implementation of schemes like **Operation Blackboard**, aimed at improving educational infrastructure.
 
• The literacy rate serves as a fundamental indicator of a country's development and is closely tied to **economic growth, social progress, and empowerment**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Key Characteristics of Literacy Rate in India**__

 
 
• **Pre-Independence Period:** Literacy rates were extremely low during British rule due to lack of focus on mass education and emphasis on elite institutions.
 
• **Post-1951 Developments:** Efforts to improve literacy included programs like **Adult Literacy Campaigns**, **Mid-Day Meal Scheme**, and **Right to Education Act (2009)**.
 
• **Regional Variations:** States like Kerala have achieved high literacy rates due to strong educational policies, while some states still face challenges in improving literacy.
